python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/northstar/research/layer_dynamics/README.md'
s=open(p).read()
def rep(old,new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old)==1, old[:80]
    s=s.replace(old,new)

rep("| Accessibility mask preset (flat, plateau, ridge, cliff, valley) | 5 presets plus size | map generator output, binary per layer per position | R1 | P1, P4 |",
"| Accessibility mask preset (flat, block, wall, barrier, lane; defined below) | 5 footprints | map generator output, binary per layer per position | R1 | P1, P4 |\n| Blocked height h: the mask blocks layers 1 to h inside the footprint | 1 to 4 | E-01 S-001 example: h = 2 | R1 | P1, P4 |")

rep("### Cross-layer rules (owner: the rule set;",
"""The terrain presets are one mechanism at five footprints. Terrain in this game is only a binary mask: each layer is open or blocked at each position (E-01 R-001-04). There are no slopes. A preset is a footprint (where layers 1 to h are blocked) and the height h; layers above h stay open everywhere. They differ by whether a unit on a blocked layer can walk around, and how far.

| Preset | Footprint | Unit on layers 1 to h, crossing it | Unit above h | What it tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flat | none: all five layers open everywhere | nothing in the way | nothing in the way | the control; no terrain effect |
| block | one compact region in the middle | goes around it, a short detour | flies straight over | high and low layers take different routes; the side that goes over can shoot down into the detour |
| wall | one long thin region across the arena, with open ends | goes around an end, a long detour | flies over | a line to hold; the flank around the end is the vulnerability |
| barrier | a region that spans the full arena width: no end to go around | cannot cross on its layer; must change layer (E-01 R-001-05, the ruling) | flies over | the terrain-forced auto-transition; with the ruling off, the unit stops at the edge |
| lane | two blocks with an open channel between them, open on all five layers | funnels through the channel | flies over the blocks or uses the channel | a choke on the low layers that the high layers bypass |

Block and wall differ only in shape (how long the detour is); barrier is the same wall made so long that there is no detour. Lane is two blocks facing each other. I kept five because each produces a different route decision; if two are not worth separate runs, merge them.

### Cross-layer rules (owner: the rule set;""")

a=s.index('### Outcomes (what a run reports)')
b=s.index('### How the map is used')
new='''### Outcomes and expected winners

A run reports: winner (A, B, stalemate, tick cap, mutual); survivors; HP-remaining ratio; cost lost per side; ticks to resolve; side and tick of first shot; first-contact tick; unanswered-fire ticks per side (ticks a side fired while the other, able to see or fire, did not); number of transitions and shots.

Each scenario carries an expected winner, stated before the run, from Westley's pillars (§2, §4). The expected winner is what a knowledgeable player would predict from the conditions alone. A run that disagrees with its expectation is first a question about the harness (check the controls), and only then a finding about the rules. Scenarios are at equal cost, count and type unless stated.

| # | Scenario | Expected winner | Basis | Outcome that proves it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X0 | Mirror: identical forces, flat, same layer, same formation | none; win rate near 0.5 | control, not a pillar | split of winners across seeds (the noise floor) |
| X1 | 10 against 5 of one type, flat | the 10 | positive control, not a pillar | winner, survivors |
| X2 | A one layer above B; A sees B; B cannot see A; A may fire down | A | "when units have a layer advantage, they can shoot without being shot back" | A's unanswered-fire ticks above 0, B's at 0 until B can see; HP-remaining ratio |
| X3 | As X2, but B sees A and cannot fire up | A | same | unanswered-fire ticks for A; B's shots 0 |
| X4 | As X2, but B sees A and can fire up at equal range and damage | none expected from the pillar; this is where the crossing v* lives | the pillar names no winner once both can answer | win rate as B's vision or fire-up value rises; the value where it crosses 0.5 |
| X5 | Same layer; A in the concave around B's line | A | "when units have a surround, the units in the concave with the surround win" | winner, HP-remaining ratio across formation and count |
| X6 | As X5 with the formations swapped | B | same | same; the mirror of X5 |
| X7 | Each side has one fragile, slow, expensive unit with a burst ability; A screens it, B leaves it exposed to fast enemies | A, as a higher win rate across seeds, not a certain win | "A player that effectively protects them has a higher chance of winning" | win rate across seeds as screen radius varies against enemy speed; burst damage landed; cost lost |
| X8 | A smaller than B, with layer advantage and concave; B a flat line | A, but only as far as the conditions carry it; the smallest count ratio at which A still wins is the measurement, not an assumption | "Organizing your units in specific patterns can lead to better engagements"; the E-01 promise that a smaller force that understands position beats a larger one | winner across count ratios; the ratio where it crosses 0.5 |
| X9 | A smaller force with one costly seer against a larger force on layers it cannot see | A, same caveat as X8 | Westley, 2026-09-23 (`Q-E12-01`), not the 2026-09-30 prompt | winner; first-contact tick; unanswered-fire ticks |

Movement checks (the auto-transition ruling across a block, wall or barrier) have no expected winner. They expect an arrival: on layer 3 at the destination with the ruling on, stopped at the edge with it off.

**Terrain presets.** The five names (flat, plateau, ridge, cliff, valley) were mine, from the plan. They appear nowhere in the bible and I never defined them, so your reaction was right. Terrain here is only a binary mask, where each layer is open or blocked at each position, so there are no slopes. The presets were one mechanism at different footprints. I renamed them and defined them in README §5 (`6709e26`):

| Preset | Footprint | Low-layer unit crossing it |
|---|---|---|
| flat | nothing | nothing in the way |
| block (was plateau) | compact region | short detour |
| wall (was ridge) | long and thin, with open ends | long detour around an end |
| barrier (was cliff) | spans the full width | no detour; it must change layer, which is what the auto-transition ruling is for |
| lane (was valley) | two blocks with an open channel between | funnels through the channel |

Units above the blocked height fly straight over any of them. I also added a blocked-height variable h (layers 1 to h blocked). Block and wall differ only in length, so merge them if you'd rather.

**Expected winners.** The doc now has scenarios X0 to X9. Each has an expected winner, stated before the run, with its basis and the outcome that proves it. The scenarios mirror your pillars:
- **X2–X4, layer advantage:** A wins while B can't see A or can't fire up. Once both can answer there is no expected winner, and that is where the lines cross.
- **X5–X6, concave:** the concave side wins, and swapping formations swaps the winner.
- **X7, protected fragile unit:** the side that protects it gets a higher win rate, not a certain win.
- **X8–X9, smaller force:** the smaller force wins only as far as its conditions carry it. The smallest winning count ratio is measured, not assumed. X9 comes from your 2026-09-23 note, not the 09-30 prompt.
- **X0–X1:** controls with no pillar behind them.

I extracted those four paragraphs to a scratch file and gave them, plus the diff, to a fresh Engineer agent. ## 3. Fixed constraints

These come from the bible and the register; the lab does not vary them unless a run says so.

- Five layers, always; layer 1 is the bottom (Q-001-01, Q-001-02). A unit is on exactly one layer at every tick.
- Terrain blocks layers at places (E-01 S-001). A unit never occupies a blocked position and layer.
- Terrain-forced auto-transition: a move order to a place blocked on the unit's layer but open on another auto-transitions it (E-01 R-001-05). The lab has an off switch for it only because a control needs an off state; the ruling itself is settled. The edges the ruling leaves open are `Q-001-04`; the lab takes the recommended reading there and can vary it.
- A transition is one transition of one duration regardless of distance (Q-002-01), by unit type (Q-004-01: Raider 1.0 s, Interceptor 1.2 s, Vanguard 2.5 s, Warden 2.0 s, Bombard 4.0 s, Bastion 5.0 s). The old layer may attack the unit until the halfway point, the new layer from the halfway point on; visibility follows the normal cross-layer sensor rules (Q-004-02). E-01 R-004-02 carries the same rule.
- Slopes (Q-004-03, Westley 2026-09-30: "Choice 2 set by the slope, no need for a switch."): a slope is a band of ground joining two layers, adjacent or not. On a slope the transition is the unit's position along it, not a timer: the time is slope length divided by unit speed, the halfway point is the slope's midline, and a unit may stop or turn back (E-01 R-001-06, R-004-06 to R-004-08). The timed rule above applies only to a transfer away from a slope. The lab builds this one way, with no timed-versus-slope switch. A unit on a slope counts as on the layer on its side of the midline (Q-004-04).
- Unit movement kinds (Q-004-04, Westley 2026-09-30): flying and swimming units change layer anywhere nothing blocks, by a timed transfer; walking units stand only where a layer has land, change layer only by walking a slope, and never rise in place (E-01 R-001-07).
- A transitioning unit may attack, in a timed transfer or on a slope, while it can see its target, and stops when the transition takes that sight away (E-01 R-004-02).
- What these rulings leave open is `Q-004-05` (which types walk, how the map marks land, cross-overs on a slope spanning several layers, the layer of a unit in a timed transfer, a walking unit given a layer order); the lab takes the recommended reading there and can vary it.
- Vision across layers shrinks with distance: production uses factor 0.50 one layer away, 0.20 two layers away, none beyond, by absolute offset in either direction (`csrc/fog.c:585`); E-01 R-005-05 says two layers below is never visible, which disagrees (`Q-005-02`), so the lab takes vision by signed offset and can test both; vantage nodes and interference zones modify it; cover blocks sight by height and never changes damage or movement (E-01 S-007).
- Production combat is same-layer only (Q-008-01). Every cross-layer rule in the lab is a hypothesis under test, not a fact about the game.
- Layer damage is weighted much more heavily than abilities and passives (Q-083-02, hub principle 4): an ability never outranks position in the lab either.
- Determinism: same seed and command stream give a byte-identical trace.

## 4. Strategic depth: the definition and four test cases

The hub definition (principle 4): the engagement's conditions, not its numbers, decide who wins. Westley's examples are from StarCraft 2; the four patterns below are their abstract form, and each is a named test case. "Expected winner" is what a knowledgeable player would predict from the conditions alone.

| Pattern | Source | Expected winner | What proves it (observables) |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 High-ground asymmetry | "when units have a layer advantage, they can shoot without being shot back" | The force with the layer advantage | Unanswered-fire ticks per side; first-shot side; HP-remaining ratio; ticks until the disadvantaged side fires |
| P2 The concave in a surround | "when units have a surround, the units in the concave with the surround win" | The side in the concave | Winner and HP-remaining ratio across formation and count; cost lost per side |
| P3 The screened glass cannon | templar are "very weak and slow and expensive, but when they use storm they're devestating to low-health units. A player that effectively protects them has a higher chance of winning" | The player who protects the fragile unit has the higher chance of winning | Win rate across seeds as screen radius varies against enemy speed; cost lost; burst damage landed |
| P4 The smaller force wins by position | "Organizing your units in specific patterns can lead to better engagements" and the promise in E-01 | The smaller force, in the configuration where position outweighs numbers | Winner with unequal counts; the smallest count ratio at which the smaller side still wins |

Depth holds for a cross-layer rule set when each pattern is true under at least one reachable configuration (one the game can produce) and none is true under every configuration. A pattern true everywhere is a dominant strategy; a pattern true nowhere is a dead mechanic.

## 5. The dimension map

Every variable an engagement in the lab has, where it lives, its range, the production value where one exists, the rung that makes it sweepable, and which depth pattern (§4) it is expected to touch. Production numbers: `csrc/om_constants.h:479-531, 560-567` (roster, category matrix, vision factors, pulse), `csrc/unit.c:84-102` (transition times), `csrc/om_constants.h:595-599` and `csrc/tactical_move.c:308` (turn rates). Damage and interval are per hit and per second as production states them; speed and range are world units per second and world units. "None" means production has no such value and the lab sets a starting one, marked lab-only.

Rungs: R0 flat combat; R1 terrain, vision, transitions, every cross-layer knob; R2 facing, formations, the storm-shaped ability; R3 sweeps and replay. A variable is fixed in the rung before the one that sweeps it.

### Unit type (owner: roster)

| Variable | Range | Production value | Rung | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HP | 100 to 1,500 | Raider 250, Interceptor 325, Vanguard 500, Warden 375, Bombard 400, Bastion 1,050 | R0 | P3, P4 |
| Damage per hit | 1 to 30 | Raider 9.0, Interceptor 6.0, Vanguard 7.5, Warden 4.0, Bombard 17.5, Bastion 7.0 | R0 | P1, P4 |
| Attack interval (s) | 0.5 to 4 | Raider 0.8, Interceptor 1.0, Vanguard 1.2, Warden 1.5, Bombard 3.0, Bastion 1.8 | R0 | P1, P2 |
| Range | 150 to 1,500 | Raider 200, Interceptor 250, Vanguard 300, Warden 350, Bombard 1,200, Bastion 800 | R0 | P1, P2 |
| Speed | 30 to 200 | Raider 150, Interceptor 130, Vanguard 80, Warden 70, Bombard 50, Bastion 40 | R0 | P3, P4 |
| Sensor radius | 300 to 1,000 | Raider 800, Interceptor 1,000, Vanguard 700, Warden 800, Bombard 300, Bastion 300 | R1 | P1 |
| Layer transition time (s) | 0.5 to 6 | Raider 1.0, Interceptor 1.2, Vanguard 2.5, Warden 2.0, Bombard 4.0, Bastion 5.0 | R1 | P1, P4 |
| Area radius | 0 to 300 | Bombard 150, all others 0 | R0 | P2, P3 |
| Category (Strike, Line, Siege) | 3 values | Raider, Interceptor Strike; Vanguard, Warden Line; Bombard, Bastion Siege | R0 | P2, P4 |
| Turn rate (rad/s) | 1 to 8 | Strike 6.0, Line 4.0, Siege 2.5, chosen by speed (Strike at 100 and above, Line at 60 and above) | R2 | P2 |
| Firing arc (degrees) | 30 to 360 | None; lab-only, 360 means no arc | R2 | P2, P3 |
| Cost | 20 to 200 | The interim power rating, HP × damage per hit / attack interval, normalized so a Vanguard is 100 (Q-074-01): Raider 90.0, Interceptor 62.4, Vanguard 100.0, Warden 32.0, Bombard 74.7, Bastion 130.7 | R0 | P3, P4 |
| Body radius (units cannot overlap) | 5 to 60 | 15 for every type (`OM_UNIT_COLLISION_RADIUS`) | R2 | P2 |
| Ability archetype: burst with windup and cooldown (the "storm" shape) | damage multiplier, radius, windup, cooldown, minimum targets | Bombard barrage: 3.0 times damage, radius 100, telegraph 30 ticks, cooldown 1,800 ticks | R2 | P3 |
| Movement kind (walking, or flying or swimming) | 2 values | none; which types walk is Q-004-05 | R1 | P1, P4 |
| Pulse-capable | yes or no | Pulse radius 500, reveal 40 ticks, cooldown 400 ticks | R1 | P1 |

The category multiplier matrix (attacker row, target column) is `OM_CATEGORY_MULTIPLIER_*`: Strike 1.0, 0.75, 1.5 against Strike, Line, Siege; Line 1.5, 1.0, 0.75; Siege 0.20, 1.5, 1.0. Area damage is capped at 4.0 times a hit (`OM_AOE_DAMAGE_CAP_MULTIPLIER`). The lab leaves out Warden aura, brace, fortify, backswing, cohort targeting and the high-load halving (production behaviours with no bearing on layer geometry); they return only if a finding needs them.

### Engagement (owner: the scenario)

| Variable | Range | Production value | Rung | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Composition per side (types) | any roster mix | none (scripted) | R0 | P2, P3, P4 |
| Count per side | 1 to 50 | none | R0 | P2, P4 |
| Formation (line, concave, box, screen, column) | 5 presets plus spacing | none | R2 | P2, P3 |
| Initial position and separation | 0 to 2,000 | none | R0 | P1, P4 |
| Initial facing (degrees) | 0 to 360 | none | R2 | P2 |
| Initial layer per group | 1 to 5 | none | R1 | P1, P4 |
| Orders (hold, move, attack-move) and destination | per group | none | R0 | P1, P4 |
| Initiative (which side moves into range) | A, B, both | none | R0 | P1, P4 |
| Initial vision (blind or pre-revealed) | 2 values | none | R1 | P1 |
| Target selection (nearest in range, focus the lowest HP, focus the highest cost) | 3 policies per side | nearest in range, same layer | R0 | P2, P3 |
| Spawn jitter and attack-phase offset | seeded | none | R0 | none (seed spread) |

### World (owner: the map)

| Variable | Range | Production value | Rung | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Accessibility mask preset (flat, block, wall, barrier, lane, ramp; defined below) | 6 footprints | map generator output, binary per layer per position | R1 | P1, P4 |
| Blocked height h: the mask blocks layers 1 to h inside the footprint | 1 to 4 | E-01 S-001 example: h = 2 | R1 | P1, P4 |
| Land per layer: where a walking unit can stand | per layer per position | none; how the map marks it is Q-004-05 | R1 | P1, P4 |
| Slopes: position, width, length, and the layers joined (adjacent or not) | length 100 to 1,000; width 100 to 600 | none in the sim; E-01 R-004-07 uses lengths 150 and 600 | R1 | P1, P4 |
| Layer spacing | 10 to 200 | none in the sim (Q-E01-01 fixes on-screen elevation only) | R1 | P1 |
| Cover discs: position, radius, height in layers | 0 to 5 layers | per E-01 S-007 | R1 | P1, P4 |
| Vantage nodes | count, radius | per E-01 S-005 | R1 | P1 |
| Interference zones | count, radius, intensity 0 to 1 | per E-01 S-005 | R1 | P1 |

Terrain in this game is a binary mask, each layer open or blocked at each position (E-01 R-001-04), plus slopes, bands of ground that join two layers, adjacent or not (E-01 R-001-06), plus where each layer has land for walking units (E-01 R-001-07). A preset is a footprint (where layers 1 to h are blocked), the height h, and the slopes on it; layers above h stay open everywhere. The presets differ by whether a unit on a blocked layer can walk around, how far, and whether a slope lets it walk up.

| Preset | Footprint | Unit on layers 1 to h, crossing it | Unit above h | What it tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flat | none: all five layers open everywhere | nothing in the way | nothing in the way | the control; no terrain effect |
| block | one compact region in the middle | goes around it, a short detour | flies straight over | high and low layers take different routes; the side that goes over can shoot down into the detour |
| wall | one long thin region across the arena, with open ends | goes around an end, a long detour | flies over | a line to hold; the flank around the end is the vulnerability |
| barrier | a region that spans the full arena width: no end to go around | cannot cross on its layer; a flying unit must change layer (E-01 R-001-05, the ruling); a walking unit cannot cross at all without a slope | flies over | the terrain-forced auto-transition; with the ruling off, the unit stops at the edge |
| lane | two blocks with an open channel between them, open on all five layers | funnels through the channel | flies over the blocks or uses the channel | a choke on the low layers that the high layers bypass |
| ramp | a barrier with one slope up its face, joining layer h to layer h+1 | walks up the slope; below the midline only the lower layer can hit it, above it only the upper layer (E-01 R-004-06) | a flying unit flies over; a walking unit on the high ground comes down only by the slope | high ground with one way up for walking units: the midline is the line to hold, and the slope's length sets how long a climber is exposed |

Block and wall differ only in shape (how long the detour is); barrier is the same wall made so long that there is no detour. Lane is two blocks facing each other. Ramp is the barrier with a slope. Each produces a different route decision; if two are not worth separate runs, merge them. No scenario in the table below uses a slope yet: the high-ground-with-a-ramp scenarios and their expected winners are still to be written.

### Cross-layer rules (owner: the rule set; the unknowns the lab exists to find)

| Variable | Range | Production value | Rung | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vision factor by signed offset (target minus observer, 9 values) | 0 to 1 each | symmetric: 1.0, 0.50, 0.20, 0, 0 at absolute offset 0 to 4 (`OM_CONE_LAYER_1_FACTOR`, `OM_CONE_LAYER_2_FACTOR`, `csrc/fog.c:585`); E-01 R-005-05 implies 0 for two below (Q-005-02) | R1 | P1 |
| Vantage vision factor by signed offset | 0 to 1 each | 1.0, 1.00, 0.40, 0.20, 0 at absolute offset 0 to 4 (E-01 R-005-06) | R1 | P1 |
| Sensor bonus per layer of elevation | 0 to 0.5 | 0.15 (`OM_ELEVATION_SENSOR_BONUS_PER_TIER`) | R1 | P1 |
| Range multiplier by signed offset (target minus attacker, 9 values) | 0 to 2 | none; same-layer only (Q-008-01) | R1 | P1 |
| Damage multiplier by signed offset | 0 to 2 | none | R1 | P1, P4 |
| Area-damage multiplier by signed offset | 0 to 2 | none | R1 | P2, P3 |
| Fire requires vision | on or off | none decided; E-01 R-007-03 lets a hidden attacker hit an observer that cannot see it, so the flag is about the attacker's own sight; the lab uses one visibility function for target choice and for the fire check | R1 | P1 |
| Facing gates fire | on or off | none | R2 | P2 |
| Halfway rule during a transition | both always targetable, per rule (old layer until halfway, new layer after), untargetable | per rule (Q-004-02); on a slope the halfway point is the midline, by position (Q-004-03) | R1 | P1, P4 |
| Terrain-forced auto-transition | on or off (off is the control) | on (E-01 R-001-05); edges per Q-001-04 | R1 | P4 |
| Movement speed during a timed transfer (not on a slope, where the unit moves at its own speed) | 0 to 1.0 times | none (mid-transition movement is unspecified in the bible beyond Q-004-02) | R1 | P1 |

### Outcomes and expected winners

A run reports: winner (A, B, stalemate, tick cap, mutual); survivors; HP-remaining ratio; cost lost per side; ticks to resolve; side and tick of first shot; first-contact tick; unanswered-fire ticks per side (ticks a side fired while the other, able to see or fire, did not); number of transitions and shots.

Each scenario carries an expected winner, stated before the run, from Westley's pillars (§2, §4). The expected winner is what a knowledgeable player would predict from the conditions alone. A run that disagrees with its expectation is first a question about the harness (check the controls), and only then a finding about the rules. Scenarios are at equal cost, count and type unless stated.

| # | Scenario | Expected winner | Basis | Outcome that proves it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X0 | Mirror: identical forces, flat, same layer, same formation | none; win rate near 0.5 | control, not a pillar | split of winners across seeds (the noise floor) |
| X1 | 10 against 5 of one type, flat | the 10 | positive control, not a pillar | winner, survivors |
| X2 | A one layer above B; A sees B; B cannot see A; A may fire down | A | "when units have a layer advantage, they can shoot without being shot back" | A's unanswered-fire ticks above 0, B's at 0 until B can see; HP-remaining ratio |
| X3 | As X2, but B sees A and cannot fire up | A | same | unanswered-fire ticks for A; B's shots 0 |
| X4 | As X2, but B sees A and can fire up at equal range and damage | none expected from the pillar; this is where the crossing v* lives | the pillar names no winner once both can answer | win rate as B's vision or fire-up value rises; the value where it crosses 0.5 |
| X5 | Same layer; A in the concave around B's line | A | "when units have a surround, the units in the concave with the surround win" | winner, HP-remaining ratio across formation and count |
| X6 | As X5 with the formations swapped | B | same | same; the mirror of X5 |
| X7 | Each side has one fragile, slow, expensive unit with a burst ability; A screens it, B leaves it exposed to fast enemies | A, as a higher win rate across seeds, not a certain win | "A player that effectively protects them has a higher chance of winning" | win rate across seeds as screen radius varies against enemy speed; burst damage landed; cost lost |
| X8 | A smaller than B, with layer advantage and concave; B a flat line | A, but only as far as the conditions carry it; the smallest count ratio at which A still wins is the measurement, not an assumption | "Organizing your units in specific patterns can lead to better engagements"; the E-01 promise that a smaller force that understands position beats a larger one | winner across count ratios; the ratio where it crosses 0.5 |
| X9 | A smaller force with one costly seer against a larger force on layers it cannot see | A, same caveat as X8 | Westley, 2026-09-23 (`Q-E12-01`), not the 2026-09-30 prompt | winner; first-contact tick; unanswered-fire ticks |

Movement checks (the auto-transition ruling across a block, wall or barrier) have no expected winner. They expect an arrival: on layer 3 at the destination with the ruling on, stopped at the edge with it off.

### How the map is used

The table is the lab's configuration surface and the axis list for §6. Each sweep picks one row as v, optionally one as w, and fixes every other row at the value the scenario states. The map is complete when every variable that the bible lets the player or the map change appears here; a variable that an experiment finds is missing is added in the same commit as the run that found it.

Status: draft, awaiting Westley's confirmation before the toy build starts.

## 6. The "lines cross" hypothesis, stated testably

Take a variable v (for example the range multiplier for fire from above) and hold every other variable fixed. The expected side's win probability is a function of v. It crosses 0.5 at some value v*. Depth exists on that axis when v* is reachable in play, meaning v* lies inside the range of values the game can produce. Now move a second variable w. Depth grows when w moves v* to another reachable value, or when w creates a second crossing, so two configurations of variables induce depth instead of one. That is Westley's "lines cross".

Pass criterion for the lab, proposed here for Westley to confirm or change (he owns it): one shared cross-layer rule set under which all four patterns of §4 hold (each true in at least one reachable configuration, none true in every configuration), with at least one crossing on a layer-rule axis and at least one two-variable interaction that adds a crossing. A separate tuned rule set per pattern does not pass.

content.content:
### S-004 — Changing layers takes time and leaves you exposed
As a commander, I want a layer change to cost time, set by the unit type for a transfer in the open and by the slope's length and my unit's speed on a slope, so that changing layers always exposes the unit and the halfway point of a slope is a line on the map I can read and hold.

Rules
- R-004-01  Given a Raider that flies or swims (R-001-07) ordered from layer 3 to layer 4 at an open position away from any slope, When the transition starts, Then the unit is on layer 4 exactly one transition duration later, with the duration taken from the unit type's transition time [Q-004-01 for the confirmed numbers; current config: Raider 1.0 s, Interceptor 1.2 s, Vanguard 2.5 s, Warden 2.0 s, Bombard 4.0 s, Bastion 5.0 s].
- R-004-02  Given a unit mid-transition, When a unit on its old layer would attack it, Then the attack may target it until the transition is halfway completed (half the duration for a timed transfer; the midline for a slope, R-004-06) and not after; and When a unit on its new layer would attack it, Then the attack may target it from the halfway point on and not before; whether either attacker sees it follows the normal cross-layer sensor rules (S-005); and the transitioning unit itself may attack, in a timed transfer or on a slope, any target it can see under the cross-layer sensor rules (S-005) and may otherwise attack (S-008), and stops attacking a target the moment the transition takes its sight of that target away.
- R-004-03  Given two units of different types ordered to the same layer at the same tick, When the faster type completes, Then the slower type is still mid-transition, and completion order always matches transition-time order.
- R-004-04  Given a unit mid-transition, When a new hard transfer to another layer is issued, Then the unit completes the current transition first and the new transfer becomes pending.
- R-004-05  Given the same seed and the same command stream, When the mission runs twice, Then every transition starts and ends on the same tick both times.
- R-004-06  Given a unit on a slope that joins layers L and L+1, When it is at any point along the slope's length, Then its transition progress is its position along the slope, not a timer: below the midline, units on layer L may attack it and units on layer L+1 may not; at or above the midline, units on layer L+1 may attack it and units on layer L may not; the same holds going up or down [Q-004-05: the same on a slope that spans more than two layers].
- R-004-07  Given a slope 600 world units long, When a Raider (speed 150) and a Bastion (speed 40) each move along it without stopping, Then the Raider takes 4.0 seconds and the Bastion 15.0 seconds; on a slope 150 long they take 1.0 and 3.75 seconds; the unit type's transition time (R-004-01) plays no part on a slope.
- R-004-08  Given a unit part-way along a slope, When the player orders it to stop or to move back the way it came, Then it stops or turns back; R-004-04's rule that a transition completes first applies only to timed transfers; while on the slope the unit counts as being on the layer on its side of the midline, for its own sensing and for what may attack it, so a unit that turns back before the midline has not changed layer and one that crosses the midline and comes back has changed twice.

Inputs: unit type transition time (per type, config); transition start tick; slope position, length and the two layers it joins (map); unit speed and position.
Outputs: unit layer field; transitioning flag and progress in the tick delta; attack eligibility.
Open flags: Q-004-05 (unit movement kinds, land, slopes that span several layers, the layer of a unit in a timed transfer).

### S-005 — Seeing across layers is worse than seeing on your own

* now - tick <= 150 and is dropped after. om_region_damage_history returns the
 * current windowed sum as the agent would read it on the next step. */
void   om_region_add_damage(om_world *w, uint32_t idx, double military_loss, double economy_loss, uint64_t tick);
double om_region_damage_history(const om_world *w, uint32_t idx);

/* ---- the world RNG contract (every card that draws follows this exactly) ----
 * One PCG32 stream per world (O'Neill PCG-XSH-RR 64/32, the reference
 * pcg32_random_r): state {uint64 state, uint64 inc}. Seeding from
 * om_world_new(seed) / om_world_set_seed(seed): inc = (seed ^ 0xDA3E39CB94B95BDBULL) << 1 | 1;
 * state = 0; step; state += seed; step. next32() is the reference output.
 * u = uniform in [0, 1) with 53 bits: a = next32() >> 5, b = next32() >> 6,
 * u = (a * 67108864.0 + b) * (1.0 / 9007199254740992.0)  (two 32-bit outputs, a then b).
 * U(lo, hi) = lo + (hi - lo) * u. randint(a, b) inclusive: n = b - a + 1,
 * threshold = (uint32_t)(-n) % n, loop r = next32() until r >= threshold,
 * return a + (r % n). triangular(lo, hi, mode): u = uniform; c = (mode - lo)/(hi - lo);
 * if u > c { u = 1 - u; c = 1 - c; swap(lo, hi); } return lo + (hi - lo) * sqrt(u * c)
 * (IEEE sqrt is correctly rounded on every platform, so it is allowed).
 * round(x) = floor(x + 0.5). Every draw consumes the stream in the order the
 * e2e file's "Draw order" paragraph states; nothing else touches the stream.
 *
 * ---- forced RNG draws (fixture) ----

# Layer lab: build spec

Written 2026-09-30 by the Architect. This is the contract the Engineer builds against, with `include/layerlab.h`. Where this file and the plan disagree, this file wins. Why the lab exists, what it must show, and the dimension map: `docs/northstar/research/layer_dynamics/README.md`. The bible rules it carries: `docs/bible/epics/E-01-layer-system.md` (rule ids below are E-01's). Register rows it follows: Q-001-03, Q-001-04, Q-004-02 to Q-004-05, Q-005-02, Q-008-01 to Q-008-03.

The lab is a research tool. It measures damage and vision relationships between layers, not pathing, so movement is deliberately crude (section 5.10). It is standalone: nothing in `csrc/` is linked or copied. Production numbers are starting values only. Two production routines are re-implemented from reference, not copied: the Taylor `sincos` (`csrc/tactical_move.c:296-306`) and the segment-disc cover test (`csrc/fog.c:265`).

## 0. Ownership and fences

- Architect owns: this file, `include/layerlab.h`, `scenarios/base.toml` values, the README in `docs/`. The Engineer does not edit them; a needed change goes back to the Architect as a question in the report.
- Engineer owns, per rung (section 11): the files that rung lists. Write fence for every spawn: `toys/layerlab/**` only. No git commands that change state; the Architect commits.
- No sub-agents. Report once, at the end, in caveman style, under 150 words: what passed, what failed, what is open.
- A test is never weakened to pass. A failing test the Engineer believes is wrong goes in the report with the reason; it is not edited around.

## 1. Layout (relative to `toys/layerlab/`)

```
include/layerlab.h          ABI (Architect)
src/ll_math.c               PCG32, Taylor sincos, helpers
src/ll_terrain.c            grid queries, slopes, flow fields (Dijkstra)
src/ll_vision.c             can_see, side visibility, pulse, cover
src/ll_move.c               goals, steering, slopes, timed transfers, separation, facing
src/ll_combat.c             acquisition, fire, damage queue, area, burst ability
src/ll_sim.c                ll_run, tick loop, termination, trace, probes
src/ll_internal.h           shared internal structs (Engineer)
Makefile
layerlab/                   Python package (import name `layerlab`)
  ffi.py scenario.py terrain.py formations.py run.py sweep.py replay.py log.py __main__.py
scenarios/base.toml  r0_raiders_10v5.toml  r2_bombard_screen.toml  (more per rung)
tests/conftest.py test_*.py
results/log.md              kept; PNG and GIF ignored (results/.gitignore)
README.md                   written in R3
```

Run everything from `toys/layerlab/`. `python3 -m layerlab ...`. Python 3.10+, numpy and matplotlib (installed); no other dependency. `tomllib` is not available on 3.10: use `tomli` if installed, else a 40-line fallback is NOT allowed: stop and report. (Check `python3 -c "import tomllib"` first; the project machine has 3.10.8, so expect to need `tomli`; if absent, report and the Architect decides.)

## 2. What is under test (the rules the sim carries)

| Rule | Where it lands |
|---|---|
| 5 layers, layer 1 bottom, one layer per unit at every tick (invariant) | `eff_layer` (5.1) |
| Terrain mask binary per layer per cell (R-001-04); a unit never occupies a blocked cell on its layer (R-001-01) | terrain (6), movement (5.10) |
| Terrain-forced auto-transition (R-001-05) and its edges (Q-001-04 reading a) | flow field (5.10) |
| Slopes (R-001-06, R-004-06 to R-004-08) | 5.9 |
| Walking vs flying (R-001-07, Q-004-04) | 5.9, 5.10 |
| Timed transfer, one duration, any distance (Q-002-01, R-004-01) | 5.8 |
| Halfway rule, transitioning units attack while they can see (R-004-02) | 5.4, 5.8, 5.9 |
| Cross-layer vision, vantage, interference, elevation bonus (R-005-01 to 07) | 5.2 |
| Pulse (R-006-01 to 05) | 5.7 |
| Cover by height, never reduces damage or movement (R-007-01 to 05) | 5.3 |
| Cross-layer fire: range, damage, area by signed offset (Q-008-03, the unknowns) | 5.4, 5.5 |

Production fidelity: where production is symmetric and E-01 says otherwise (R-005-05, Q-005-02) the lab runs production's symmetric table by default and takes vision by signed offset so the asymmetric reading is one table edit.

## 3. Defaults (`scenarios/base.toml`)

Everything below is the default; a scenario overrides by deep-merge. Types carry production numbers (`csrc/om_constants.h`), `movement_kind = "fly"` for all six (Q-004-05 reading a1), cost computed by the power rating: `cost = hp * dmg / interval / 31.25` (Vanguard = 100; Q-074-01) unless the type sets `cost` explicitly, `body_radius = 15`, `arc_deg = 360`, `turn_rate` 6.0 / 4.0 / 2.5 for Strike / Line / Siege.

| Type | cat | hp | dmg | interval | range | speed | sensor | transition_s | aoe_r |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| raider | Strike | 250 | 9.0 | 0.8 | 200 | 150 | 800 | 1.0 | 0 |
| interceptor | Strike | 325 | 6.0 | 1.0 | 250 | 130 | 1000 | 1.2 | 0 |
| vanguard | Line | 500 | 7.5 | 1.2 | 300 | 80 | 700 | 2.5 | 0 |
| warden | Line | 375 | 4.0 | 1.5 | 350 | 70 | 800 | 2.0 | 0 |
| bombard | Siege | 400 | 17.5 | 3.0 | 1200 | 50 | 300 | 4.0 | 150 |
| bastion | Siege | 1050 | 7.0 | 1.8 | 800 | 40 | 300 | 5.0 | 0 |
| caster (lab-only) | Line | 120 | 4.0 | 1.5 | 450 | 55 | 700 | 3.0 | 0 |

`caster`: ability burst, `ab_dmg_mult = 6.0`, `ab_radius = 120`, `ab_windup_s = 1.5`, `ab_cooldown_s = 12.0`, `ab_min_targets = 3`, `cost = 150` (explicit: expensive, per the strategic-depth pillar). Lab-only; it stands in for the storm shape and is not a game unit.

Rules defaults: `vis_factor = [0, 0, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 0.5, 0.2, 0, 0]`; `vantage_vis_factor = [0, 0.2, 0.4, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.4, 0.2, 0]`; `sensor_elev_bonus_per_layer = 0.15`; `range_mult = dmg_mult = aoe_layer_mult = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0]` (same-layer only, Q-008-01: cross-layer fire is off until a scenario turns it on); `category_mult` rows (attacker) Strike `[1.0, 0.75, 1.5]`, Line `[1.5, 1.0, 0.75]`, Siege `[0.20, 1.5, 1.0]`; `aoe_cap_mult = 4.0`; `pulse_radius = 500`, `pulse_reveal_s = 2.0`, `pulse_cooldown_s = 20.0`; `transition_speed_mult = 1.0`; `separation_weight = 0.5`; `spawn_jitter = 10`; flags `fire_requires_vision = 1`, `facing_gates_fire = 0`, `halfway_mode = 1 (rule)`, `auto_transition = 1`, `cover_mode = 1`, `chase_when_idle = 0`, `forced_change_penalty = 100000`, `timed_new_layer_at_half = 1`; `max_ticks = 6000`, `stalemate_ticks = 400`. Terrain default: 80 x 40 cells of 50 units (arena 4000 x 2000), preset `flat`, `layer_spacing = 0`.

## 4. The knobs the lab sweeps

The `ll_rules` fields and the unit-type fields are the sweep surface. Any scalar is swept by dotted path (section 8). The ones the experiments lean on: `rules.range_mult[i]`, `rules.dmg_mult[i]`, `rules.aoe_layer_mult[i]`, `rules.vis_factor[i]`, `rules.vantage_vis_factor[i]`, `rules.sensor_elev_bonus_per_layer`, `rules.layer_spacing` via `terrain.layer_spacing`, `rules.halfway_mode`, `rules.auto_transition`, `rules.forced_change_penalty`, `types.<name>.<field>`, group counts, formation parameters, terrain preset parameters. A path that does not resolve is an error, never ignored.

## 5. Tick and behavior

One tick is 1/20 s, `dt = 0.05`. Iteration is always in index order (unit id = index in `spawns`); no hash order, no pointer order, no wall clock.

### 5.1 Effective layer
`u.layer` is the layer the unit counts as being on. It is recomputed at the start of every tick (step 2) from the unit's movement state:
- Not changing layer: its layer.
- Timed transfer from L0 to L1, elapsed `e`, duration `D = transition_s`: L0 while `e < D/2`; from `D/2` on, L1 if `timed_new_layer_at_half` else L0 until `e >= D`, then L1.
- On a slope with bottom layer `B`, top `T`, `n = T - B`, position `t` in [0,1]: `B + count of k in 1..n with t >= (k - 0.5) / n`. At the midline of a one-layer slope the unit counts as upper (R-004-06 "at or above"). Direction (up or down) does not matter.

A unit is `changing` while in a timed transfer or on a slope.

### 5.2 Vision
`can_see(o, t)` (observer alive; both layers effective):
1. `off = LL_OFFS(o.layer, t.layer)`. `f = in_vantage(o) ? vantage_vis_factor[off] : vis_factor[off]`. `in_vantage`: observer xy inside any vantage disc (any layer). If `f <= 0`, false.
2. `interf` = sum over zones with `zone.layer == o.layer` and `d < r` of `intensity * (1 - d / r)`, clamped to [0,1] (d xy distance from observer to zone centre).
3. `elev = max(0, 1 + sensor_elev_bonus_per_layer * (o.layer - t.layer))`.
4. `eff_r = o.sensor * (1 - interf) * elev * f`.
5. `d3 = sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2 + (dl * layer_spacing)^2)`, `dl = o.layer - t.layer` (with spacing 0 this is xy distance). Visible if `d3 <= eff_r`.
6. If `cover_mode`, not blocked (5.3).

Side visibility, computed once per tick (step 3) into `side_sees[side][unit]`: unit `e` is seen by side `S` if any alive unit of `S` `can_see(e)`, or `e.pre_revealed` and `e.side != S`, or a pulse of side `S` covers it (5.7). Target acquisition and the fire check both read `side_sees`; there is no second visibility function.

`ll_probe_can_see(sc, seed, o, t)` runs spawn placement and evaluates step 5.2 for the pair at tick 0 (`can_see` only, no side union).

### 5.3 Cover (R-007-01 to 05)
With `cover_mode = 1`, a disc blocks the sight line from `o` to `t` when: neither endpoint's xy is inside the disc (`dist <= r`); the closest point of the xy segment to the disc centre, at parameter `s` in [0,1], is closer than `r`; and `lerp(o.layer, t.layer, s) <= height_layer`. R-007-01 (both on 1, height 2) blocks; R-007-02 (both on 3) does not. Cover never changes damage, movement or fire: a hidden attacker still fires at an observer it can see (R-007-03); the cover test is applied only inside `can_see`. The layer interpolation is the lab's choice for cross-layer lines; it is recorded as T1-candidate and may be varied by `cover_mode` values added later.

### 5.4 Acquisition and eligibility
For every alive unit `u` in index order, candidates are alive enemies `e` with:
- visibility: `side_sees[u.side][e]`, unless `fire_requires_vision = 0`.
- `off = LL_OFFS(u.layer, e.layer)` and `range_mult[off] > 0` and `dmg_mult[off] > 0` (area units: `aoe_layer_mult[off] > 0`).
- halfway eligibility, if `e` is changing: `halfway_mode = RULE`: only attackers whose `u.layer == e.layer` (the effective layer) may target it, with `off = 4`; `BOTH`: attackers on either endpoint layer of the change (timed: from and to; slope: bottom and top) as if same layer (`off = 4`); `UNTARGETABLE`: none.
- range: `d3 <= u.range * range_mult[off]`.
- if `facing_gates_fire`: the bearing to `e` lies within `arc_deg / 2` of the facing (dot product against `cos(arc/2)`, 5.12).

A changing unit may itself acquire and fire on any candidate its own effective layer allows (R-004-02: it stops only when the transition takes its sight away, which falls out of `side_sees`: if that side no longer sees the target it is not a candidate).

Selection: policy `NEAREST` (smallest `d3`), `LOWEST_HP` (smallest absolute HP), `HIGHEST_COST` (largest type cost); ties break nearest, then lowest index.

A unit under a `MOVE` order that has not arrived does not acquire or fire. Units in an ability windup do not fire.

### 5.5 Fire and damage
Each unit has a cooldown; `cooldown -= dt` each tick (step 1). It fires when it has a target, `cooldown <= 0`, and nothing above forbids it. Firing sets `cooldown += interval_s`. Initial cooldown is drawn at spawn: `U(0, interval_s)`.

All firing decisions in a tick are made before any damage applies (simultaneous fire; a unit killed this tick still fires). Events are queued and applied together in step 6:
- Direct (`aoe_r == 0`): `dmg * category_mult[a.cat][t.cat] * dmg_mult[off]` to the target.
- Area (`aoe_r > 0`): centre = target xy at fire time. Every alive enemy within `aoe_r` (xy) of the centre that passes halfway eligibility takes `dmg * category_mult * aoe_layer_mult[LL_OFFS(attacker.layer, e.layer)]`. Per target per tick, the sum of area damage is clamped to `aoe_cap_mult` times the largest single area hit it took that tick. No friendly fire.
- Burst ability (5.6) damage is applied in the same step and is not capped.

Damage dealt is counted after clamping to the target's remaining HP. A unit with `hp <= 0` after step 6 is dead; its type cost is added to `cost_lost[side]`.

### 5.6 Burst ability (the storm shape)
A unit with `ability_kind = BURST`, not winding, with ability cooldown `<= 0`: looks at visible, eligible enemies within `range`; for each, counts eligible enemies within `ab_radius` (xy) of it; takes the one with the largest count (ties nearest, then lowest index). If the count is `>= ab_min_targets`, it locks that enemy's xy as the centre and starts a windup of `ab_windup_s`; during the windup the unit does not move or fire. At expiry every alive enemy within `ab_radius` of the locked centre (enemies may have left; that is the counterplay) takes `dmg * ab_dmg_mult * aoe_layer_mult[off]` (no category multiplier); the ability cooldown starts at expiry. A caster that dies in its windup casts nothing. A cast counts as one shot.

### 5.7 Pulse (R-006)
A `pulse_capable` unit with `spawn.pulse_tick >= 0` pulses on that tick if its cooldown is ready. For `pulse_reveal_s` seconds after, its side sees every alive enemy on any layer within `pulse_radius * (1 - interf_at_pulser)` (xy) of the pulser's current position, if the pulser is alive. Cooldown `pulse_cooldown_s` from the pulse tick. No heuristic trigger.

### 5.8 Timed transfer (flyers only)
Started by `spawn.transfer_layer` at `transfer_tick`, or by a forced change (5.10). Walkers never make timed transfers. A transfer to the unit's own layer completes at once with no transition. Otherwise: duration `transition_s` whatever the distance (Q-002-01); the target layer must be open at the unit's xy when it starts (else it stays pending and starts on the first tick it is, R-002-02). During the transfer the unit moves at `speed * transition_speed_mult` and may enter only cells open on both layers (else it stands). A new transfer ordered mid-transfer becomes pending and starts when the current completes (R-004-04). The unit's `transitions` counter increments each time its effective layer value changes.

### 5.9 Slopes and walking (R-001-06, R-001-07, R-004-06 to 08)
Flyers ignore slopes: they are terrain, not paths, for them. Walkers occupy only cells where `land` has their layer's bit, and change layer only by walking a slope.

A walker mounts a slope when its flow-field step says to take it and it is within `max(body_radius, 0.5 * cell)` of the matching edge centre; it is placed at the edge centre, `t = 0` (bottom) or `1` (top). On a slope it moves along the slope direction at its own speed (`speed`, never `transition_s`; R-004-07: 600 units at speed 150 takes exactly 80 ticks, at speed 40 exactly 300 ticks), lateral position fixed on the centre line, no separation push. Each tick it compares the flow field's cost-to-go at the two edge nodes and moves toward the cheaper one (ties keep the current direction), so a changed goal turns it back (R-004-08); a unit with no goal (hold) stops where it is. It dismounts at `t >= 1` or `t <= 0` onto the edge's layer and cell. Its layer while on the slope is 5.1. Eligibility while on a slope is 5.4 with `changing` true.

### 5.10 Movement (deliberately crude; transfer class T3)
Per tick, per unit not winding and not on a slope: a goal point is chosen. `HOLD`: none (with `chase_when_idle`, the nearest visible enemy this unit could hit if in range, as for `ATTACK_MOVE`). `MOVE`: the order goal; arrival within `1.5 * body_radius`, after which the unit behaves as `HOLD`. `ATTACK_MOVE`: if a visible enemy it could hit exists and is out of range, its position (chase), but if some candidate is already in range the unit stands and fires; otherwise the order goal.

Path: if the straight segment to the goal is clear (sampled every half cell; each sampled cell open on the unit's layer, and `land` for a walker) the unit steers straight. Otherwise it follows a flow field. A flow field is a Dijkstra cost-to-go from the goal over nodes `(cell, layer)`, cached by `(goal cell, movement kind, auto_transition)`:
- same-layer edges to the 8 neighbours, cost = distance, allowed if the neighbour cell is open on that layer (and `land` for walkers; no diagonal corner cutting through a blocked cell);
- flyers, if `auto_transition`: a layer-change edge `(cell, L) -> (cell, M)` for every `M != L` open at that cell, cost `forced_change_penalty * |M - L|` (so a detour on the current layer beats any change, and the nearest open layer is the cheapest change; ties go to the lower layer). With `auto_transition = 0` there are no layer-change edges and a blocked destination leaves the unit standing at the edge;
- walkers: a slope edge between the two edge nodes, cost = slope length, both directions;
- goal nodes: every layer on which the goal cell is open (and land for walkers). If the goal cell has none, the goal snaps to the nearest cell that is open on the unit's current layer by centre distance, and the unit stops there (R-001-05 second clause).

A step whose next node changes layer starts a forced timed transfer to that layer at the current xy (5.8) and the unit keeps following the field. Steering is toward the next node's cell centre. Movement is axis-separated against blocked cells (try the full step, then x, then y). After movement, same-layer separation: for pairs `i < j` both not on a slope, effective layers equal, `overlap = r_i + r_j - d > 0`: each is pushed apart by `overlap / 2 * separation_weight` along the pair axis (along +x if `d == 0`); a push into a blocked cell is skipped.

### 5.11 Termination and outcomes
After step 6: a side with no alive units loses; both empty the same tick is `MUTUAL`. Otherwise `STALEMATE` after `stalemate_ticks` consecutive ticks with no damage applied; `CAP` at `max_ticks`. `ticks` is the number of ticks run.
- `hp_ratio[s]`: remaining HP of side `s` over its starting HP. `survivors`, `cost_lost`, `damage_dealt`, `shots` per side. `transitions`: total across units.
- `first_shot_side/tick`: the first tick any shot is fired (ties: both sides fired that tick: side 0 is recorded, and `first_shot_side = 2` is not used; the tie is visible in the trace).
- `first_contact_tick`: first tick on which any `side_sees` entry is set for an alive enemy.
- `unanswered_ticks[s]`: ticks on which side `s` fired at least one shot and side `1 - s` fired none, counted only while both sides have alive units.
- `unit[i]`: final xy, hp, layer, alive, transitions.

### 5.12 Numerics
Doubles only. `sqrt` is allowed (IEEE correctly rounded); no other libm call in the sim path (`sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `pow`, `exp` are banned). Facing is stored as a unit vector. `sincos` is the production Taylor series (7 terms, argument wrapped to [-pi, pi]): used to turn `facing_deg`, `arc_deg / 2` and the per-tick turn step into vectors and cosines. Turning: if `dot(facing, desired) >= cos(step)` snap to desired, else rotate by `step = turn_rate * dt` toward desired using the sign of the cross product. Arc test: `dot(facing, bearing) >= cos(arc / 2)`; `arc_deg >= 360` skips the test.

### 5.13 RNG
PCG32 exactly as the contract at `csrc/ouroboros_sim.h:310-322` (reference `pcg32_random_r`; `inc = (seed ^ 0xDA3E39CB94B95BDBULL) << 1 | 1`, `state = 0`, step, `state += seed`, step; `u` from two outputs with 53 bits; `U(lo, hi) = lo + (hi - lo) * u`). The only draws, in this order, per spawn in index order: jitter x `U(-j, j)`, jitter y `U(-j, j)`, initial cooldown `U(0, interval_s)`. Nothing else touches the stream. (The re-implementation follows the written contract; it does not copy production code.)

## 6. Terrain presets (`layerlab/terrain.py`)

A preset builds `open` and `land` arrays and the slope list from parameters. `open` bit `L-1` is set unless the preset blocks layer `L` there; `land` defaults to equal `open` (every open layer is a deck a walker can stand on) except as stated. Arena `W x H` in cells; `h` = blocked height (layers `1..h` blocked inside the footprint); strips are defined by x.
- `flat`: all open, all land.
- `block`: a rectangle `bw x bh` cells at the arena centre, layers `1..h` blocked, `land` cleared on those layers there.
- `wall`: a strip `wt` cells thick in x across the arena centre, spanning y from `end_gap` cells from the bottom to `end_gap` cells from the top (open ends), layers `1..h` blocked.
- `barrier`: a strip `wt` cells thick in x spanning the full y range, layers `1..h` blocked.
- `lane`: two blocks above and below a channel `ch` cells wide at the arena's mid-y, each spanning a strip `wt` thick in x, layers `1..h` blocked; channel open on all layers.
- `ramp`: a barrier from `x1` to the arena's far edge (the plateau), layers `1..h` blocked there; `land` inside the plateau only on layers `h+1..5`; ground layer `g` (default 1): outside the plateau `land` only on layer `g`... (see below); one slope on the plateau's face at mid-y: bottom edge centre `(x1*cell, mid-y)` on layer `g`, direction `+x`, length `sl`, width `sw`, top layer `h+1` (spans `h+1-g` layers). The slope's top edge must land inside the plateau on layer `h+1`; the preset asserts it. For `ramp`, outside the plateau `land` is set only on layer `g` and on all layers above `h+1`... no: set `land` outside the plateau to exactly layer `g`; walkers outside it live on `g`; flyers ignore `land`.

Every preset validates: spawns land on open (and land for walkers) cells; slope edge cells are `land` on their layers; slope footprints do not overlap. Violations raise before the C call.

## 7. Formations (`layerlab/formations.py`)

Return `(x, y, facing_deg)` per unit for `n` units; parameters per group. `line`: perpendicular to the group's facing, `spacing` apart, centred at `(x, y)`. `column`: along the facing. `box`: `cols` wide grid. `concave`: units on a circle of radius `R` around `center = (cx, cy)` (the enemy's centre), spanning `arc_deg` centred on the bearing from `center` to the group's `(x, y)`, each facing `center`. `screen`: `n_screen` units on a circle of radius `screen_r` around the group's `(x, y)` (the protected unit stands at `(x, y)`), facing outward, spanning `arc_deg` centred on the enemy bearing; the protected unit is a separate group. `spacing` default is `2.5 * body_radius`. Placement is pure geometry: no draws.

## 8. Python driver

- `ffi.py`: ctypes mirror of the header; at import, assert `ll_abi_version() == 1` and `ll_sizeof(i)` equals `ctypes.sizeof` for each mirrored struct; builds nothing (the Makefile builds `build/liblayerlab.so`; `tests/conftest.py` runs `make` once).
- `scenario.py`: loads a TOML with `extends = "base.toml"` (deep merge of dicts, lists replaced); schema: `[rules]`, `[types.<name>]` (field overrides; `movement_kind = "fly" | "walk"`, `category = "strike" | "line" | "siege"`, `cost` optional), `[terrain]` (`preset`, preset parameters, `layer_spacing`, optional `[[terrain.cover]]`, `[[terrain.vantage]]`, `[[terrain.zone]]`, `[[terrain.slope]]`), `[[groups]]` (`side = "A" | "B"`, `type`, `count`, `formation` and its parameters, `x`, `y`, `facing`, `layer`, `order`, `goal = [x, y]`, `pre_revealed`, `transfer_layer`, `transfer_tick`, `pulse_tick`, `target_policy`), `[run]` (`max_ticks`, `stalemate_ticks`). `set_path(scn, "rules.range_mult[5]", v)` and `groups[0].count` style dotted-index paths; an unresolvable path raises `KeyError`. `to_c(scn) -> ll_scenario` and a `scenario_diff(a, b)` returning the changed dotted paths (used by the log).
- `run.py`: `run(scn, seed=0, trace=False) -> Result` (dataclass of the `ll_result` fields plus optional numpy trace array of shape `(ticks, n_units)` with the 20-byte record dtype). `expected_win(result, expect: "A" | "B") -> 1.0 | 0.5 | 0.0` is NOT defined: a win is `winner == expect` (1.0), anything else 0.0, and stalemate/cap counts are reported separately.
- `sweep.py`: `sweep(scn, var, values, seeds=range(5), var2=None, values2=None, metric="win_rate", expect="A") -> SweepTable`. Metrics: `win_rate`, `hp_ratio_A`, `hp_ratio_B`, `ticks`, `unanswered_A`, `unanswered_B`, `cost_lost_A`, `cost_lost_B`. Prints a fixed-width table (one line per value; a matrix for two variables) with mean over seeds, the count of stalemates and caps, and the seed range; saves a matplotlib PNG to `results/` (line plus per-seed scatter; heatmap for two variables); `find_crossings(xs, ys, level=0.5)` returns the interpolated x where the series crosses the level, in order; the table prints them. Appends to `results/log.md` through `log.py`.
- `log.py`: `append(entry)`; each entry carries date, the command line, `scenario_diff` against `base.toml`, the table, the PNG path, and a transfer class (`T1`, `T2`, `T3`; section 12) that the caller must pass (no default).
- `replay.py`: `replay(trace, terrain)` as `matplotlib.animation.FuncAnimation`: top-down view, colour per side, marker shape per type category, layer keys `1` to `5` filter or highlight a layer, HP bars, hollow marker while changing layer, slopes drawn as bands with the midline, `save_gif(path)`. No other graphics library (pygame is not installed).
- `__main__.py`: `python3 -m layerlab run <scenario.toml> [--seed N] [--set path=value ...]`, `sweep <scenario.toml> --var path --values a,b,c [--var2 ... --values2 ...] [--seeds N] [--metric m] [--expect A|B] [--class T1|T2|T3]`, `replay <scenario.toml> [--seed N] [--gif path]`.

## 9. Build and determinism

`Makefile` builds `build/liblayerlab.so` from `src/*.c`. Flags: `-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -fPIC -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno`, plus `-msse2 -mfpmath=sse -fexcess-precision=standard` only when `uname -m` is `x86_64` (they fail on this arm64 Mac). Targets: `all` (O2), `O0`, `O2` (separate dirs `build/O0`, `build/O2`), `clean`. `OPT` and `WERROR` variables as in the root Makefile. The Makefile and `src/*.c` produce no warnings with `WERROR=1`.

Determinism gate: the same scenario and seed twice give identical `ll_result` bytes and identical trace bytes; the O0 and O2 builds give identical trace bytes; different seeds differ (jitter and cooldown draws).

## 10. Tests (`tests/`, pytest; `conftest.py` builds the lib once)

Each test's docstring names the E-01 rule or register row it mirrors. Positive control for every detector.

1. Determinism: twice identical; O0 vs O2 identical; seeds 0 and 1 differ.
2. Positive control: `r0_raiders_10v5` (10 vs 5 raiders, flat, same layer, attack-move): A wins on 20 of 20 seeds. Mirror (5 vs 5 identical, same formation): winners split across 20 seeds with each side winning at least 4.
3. Negative control: A on layer 5, B on layer 1, default (cross-layer off), `fire_requires_vision = 1`: `winner = STALEMATE`, `damage_dealt = [0, 0]`, `shots = [0, 0]`, `first_contact_tick = -1`.
4. `can_see` isolation on R-005-01 to 07's numbers (observer sensor 1000 on layer 3; enemy layer 3 at 900, layer 4 at 400 and 600, layer 5 at 150 and 250, layer 1 at any distance with the default table, vantage case, interference 0.5 case), via `ll_probe_can_see`, with a positive and a negative case each. R-005-05 is run twice: default (symmetric table; two layers below at 150 is visible) and the asymmetric table (zero for offsets 2 below), both as explicit tests naming `Q-005-02`.
5. Cover: R-007-01 and R-007-02; a disc that contains an endpoint does not hide it; cover never changes damage (same scenario with `cover_mode` 0 and 1 and the observer able to see in both: identical damage totals).
6. Halfway rule from both sides: a flyer in a timed transfer from layer 3 to 4 (`transition_s = 2`), with a same-layer attacker on 3 and another on 4: the layer-3 attacker fires at it before 1.0 s (tick 20) and not after; the layer-4 attacker the reverse; `halfway_mode` 0 and 2 change this as defined. The changing unit itself fires at a visible target and stops when the target leaves its sight.
7. Auto-transition ruling: a `barrier` with `h = 2`; a flying raider on layer 1 ordered across: `auto_transition = 1` arrives on layer 3 (nearest open layer) and was in a timed transfer at the strip's near edge; `= 0` stops at the edge. With `forced_change_penalty = 0` and an open end shorter than the transfer cost, it takes the shorter route (Q-001-04 b); with 100000 it takes the detour (a). A destination blocked on every layer: the unit stops as close as it can on its layer.
8. Slopes: `ramp` with `h = 1`, `sl = 600`: a walking raider (speed 150) takes 80 ticks (+/- 1) from mounting to dismount, a walking bastion (speed 40) 300 ticks (R-004-07); on a 150-long slope 20 and 75. Eligibility: below the midline an attacker on the lower layer may target the climber and one on the upper layer may not; at and above the midline the reverse (R-004-06). Turn back: a walker given a goal that reverses before the midline dismounts at the bottom with `transitions = 0`; after the midline it ends with `transitions = 2` (R-004-08). A walker at a `barrier` with no slope never crosses. A flyer ignores the slope and crosses by timed transfer. A slope spanning two layers (`h = 2`, `g = 1`): two cross-overs at `t = 0.25` and `0.75`.
9. Area damage: bombard against a 3-unit cluster, `aoe_layer_mult` zero for off-layer neighbours: only same-layer units are hit; the per-target cap holds (4 bombards firing on one tick deal at most `4.0 x` one hit to a target).
10. Burst ability: `caster` against 3 clustered raiders deals `dmg * 6.0` to each inside the locked centre at expiry; a target that left the radius during the windup takes nothing; a caster killed in its windup casts nothing.
11. Arc gate (R2): a unit facing away does not fire with `facing_gates_fire = 1` and does with `= 0`; it turns at `turn_rate`.
12. Crossing detector: `find_crossings` on a synthetic sigmoid returns the known crossing within 1e-9 (positive control); on a flat series returns none (negative control); the count-ratio sweep (1:2 to 2:1 of equal forces on flat) shows a crossing between 0.8 and 1.25 (positive control from the README).
13. Speed gate: 20 v 20 raiders, a 25-value sweep x 5 seeds completes in under 20 s on this machine; the test prints the time.

## 11. Rungs (one Engineer spawn each; the Architect reviews before the next)

| Rung | Content | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| R0 | `ll_math.c`, `ll_sim.c` (loop, spawn, RNG, termination, trace), `ll_combat.c` (nearest target, direct fire, same-layer area, category matrix, cooldown), flat `ll_move.c` (straight steering, attack-move, hold, move, separation), `ll_terrain.c` stub (flat grid queries), `ll_vision.c` (sensor radius, same-layer only, `side_sees`), Makefile, `ffi.py`, `scenario.py`, `run.py`, `scenarios/base.toml`, `scenarios/r0_raiders_10v5.toml`, tests 1 and 2. All header fields exist; layer-related ones are inert (read, validated, unused). | `make -C toys/layerlab && python3 -m pytest toys/layerlab/tests -q` green for tests 1 and 2; Makefile warning-free at `WERROR=1`; a 10 v 5 run prints a result |
| R1 | `ll_terrain.c` (masks, land, slopes, Dijkstra flow fields, straight-segment clear test), `ll_vision.c` (all of 5.2, 5.3, 5.7), `ll_move.c` (timed transfers, forced change, slopes, walkers), `ll_combat.c` (all cross-layer knob sites, halfway eligibility), `terrain.py`, presets `flat block wall barrier lane ramp`, scenario terrain schema; tests 3 to 9 | tests 1 to 9 green |
| R2 | facing, turn, arc gate; `formations.py`; burst ability; `r2_bombard_screen.toml`; tests 10 and 11 | tests 1 to 11 green |
| R3 | `sweep.py`, `replay.py`, `log.py`, CLI, `README.md` (how to run a run, a sweep, a replay; the knob table), first log entries from the controls (test 12 sweep, X0, X1); test 12 and 13 | tests 1 to 13 green; `results/log.md` has the count-ratio crossing entry |

R0 is two passes: C first, then driver and tests. Each pass reports separately.

## 12. Transfer classes (every log entry and PNG title carries one)

- **T1** rule geometry that ports to the game as is: vision tables, cover-height LOS, the halfway rule, slope midline eligibility, offset multipliers, area splash, arcs.
- **T2** magnitudes whose direction transfers but whose numbers retune: win rates, HP ratios, ticks, cost lost. The lab has no economy, no Warden aura, brace, fortify, backswing or cohort targeting, no high-load halving, and fog is symmetric.
- **T3** lab-only: steering, the coarse flow fields, formation drift, pulse timing, the stalemate window.

## 13. Not built

Layer preference (S-003), hard-transfer rejection and era masks (S-011), commands during a run, per-faction fog, economy, `Q-004-05` choices other than reading (a) (the knobs that exist for them are `timed_new_layer_at_half` and the `movement_kind` per type), and any rendering beyond the matplotlib replay.
